records.summary: 1.The Puzzle Door: •The party encounters a door locked by a complex riddle or mechanical puzzle. Solving the puzzle requires Intelligence checks (DC 15), but a failed attempt may activate a trap. 2.The Guardian Awakes: •A massive golem or ancient creature awakens as the players disturb the templeʼs treasures. They can fight, negotiate, or flee through the labyrinthine corridors.

1.Tunnel Types: •Sewage Canals: Waste-filled channels that carry foul water. Crossing these canals requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12) to avoid slipping or falling into the waste. •Crumbling Catacombs: Narrow, unstable passages lined with ancient bones and burial alcoves. The slightest vibration can trigger a collapse. •Hidden Sanctuaries: Secret chambers within the catacombs, often used for forbidden rituals or by thieves hiding their loot. •Maintenance Rooms: Some areas of the sewers have old pump rooms or storage areas, offering potential shelter but also attracting scavengers. 2.Lighting and Atmosphere: •Complete Darkness: Most areas lack light, forcing players to rely on torches or magical light sources. Without them, movement and combat are made with disadvantage. •Foul Air and Fog: Some areas are filled with noxious fumes. Players exposed to these gases must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 13) or become poisoned for 1 hour. •Dripping Water and Echoes: Sounds echo unpredictably through the tunnels, making it hard to judge distance or direction. Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 15) are needed to pinpoint the source of noises. 3.Terrain and Conditions: •Slick Floors: The damp conditions create slippery surfaces. Players moving at normal speed must succeed on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid slipping. •Collapsed Passages: Some tunnels are blocked by rubble. Clearing a path requires a successful Strength (Athletics) check (DC 15) and 1d4 hours of work. •Rotting Bridges and Ladders: Old wooden structures may break under stress, requiring Dexterity saves (DC 12) to avoid falling into waste or deeper pits.
1.Toxic Gas Pockets: •Certain areas are filled with invisible gas. Players must succeed on Constitution saves (DC 14) or take 2d8 poison damage and become incapacitated for 1 minute.
Long rests are risky unless a sanctified area is found. Players resting without protection must make Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 15) to avoid surprise attacks from roaming creatures or spirits.

1.Navigating the Maze: •Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 15) are required to avoid getting lost. A failed check forces the party to backtrack, wasting time and risking additional encounters.
Short rests are possible in dry, safe corners of the temple, but players must remain wary of guardians. Roll a d20 each hour of rest; on a result of 5 or lower, an encounter interrupts the rest.

1.Mirror Traps: •Illusionary mirrors mislead adventurers into dead ends or dangerous chambers. A successful Intelligence (Investigation) check (DC 13) spots the illusion. 2.Gas Chambers: •Entering certain rooms triggers a poisonous gas cloud. Players must succeed on Constitution saves (DC 14) to avoid taking 3d8 poison damage. 3.Ancient Ambush: •Creatures hidden within statues or behind walls leap out to attack intruders. A failed Perception check (DC 15) results in a surprise attack.

Effect: Once per short rest, when you succeed on an Insight check against a creature, you may immediately attempt a Suggestion-like effect (as per the spell, but non-magical and Charisma-based). Upgrade (500 XP): You may use this ability twice per short rest, and targets have disadvantage if youʼve used Surface Scan or Mental Signature on them in the past day. 🐍 TIER 3: Serpentʼs Will (XP Cost: 1,600, requires 2 Tier 2 abilities)
When a Serpent enters a volatile or emotionally charged location, their presence may cause unintended Dissonance modulation.

Your psychic field projects unease. As a minor action, you may activate your Dissonant Presence. While active, creatures of your choice within 10 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + Proficiency + Charisma modifier) or gain disadvantage on Insight, Perception, and Charisma- based checks for 1 minute. This ability may be used a number of times per long rest equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

Effect: Once per long rest, you can force a creature within 60 ft to feel a powerful emotional override (fear, sorrow, rage, joy, or peace). They must succeed on a Wisdom save or be compelled to act accordingly (GM interprets emotional shift).
Once per long rest, when you succeed on a saving throw against being frightened or charmed, you may grant an ally within 10 feet advantage on their next save against the same effect.

Effect: After 1 minute of conversation or proximity, you can attune to a creature's mental presence. You can detect them within 100 ft through walls or illusions. Upgrade (300 XP): If you are within 30 ft, you gain advantage on saving throws against any effects they use against you. 🌀 TIER 2: Subtle Dominion (XP Cost: 800, requires 2 Tier 1 abilities)

Effect: Once per long rest, when you succeed on a Wisdom or Charisma saving throw, you may rebound the effect to its source (if it is psychic, fear, charm, or emotional in nature). Bonus: Gain temporary HP equal to your Charisma modifier. Upgrade (700 XP): You may use this ability twice per long rest. 🐉 TIER 4: Dragonsa Initiate (XP Cost: 3,200, requires 2 Tier 3 abilities)

Effect: You can read the surface emotions of any creature you can see within 30 ft. This does not reveal thoughts, only emotional state. Bonus: Advantage on one Deception, Persuasion, or Intimidation check per use. Upgrade (200 XP): You may also detect if the target is under mental control or magical influence.

You instinctively feel the moods of nearby allies. Once per long rest, you may alert all allies within 30 ft of unseen danger, granting them advantage on their next initiative roll or Perception check.

Effect: As an action, target one creature within 60 ft. On a failed Wisdom save, they take 2d6 psychic damage and suffer disadvantage on their next mental save. Upgrade (400 XP): Damage increases to 3d6. On a success, target still suffers half damage and no disadvantage.

Rival gangs control certain sections of the megacity, especially lower levels. Roll a d20 every hour

Every few minutes, gravitational pulses shift objects toward or away from the center of convergence. Characters and ships caught in a pulse must make Strength saving throws (DC 15) or be dragged toward a wormhole or rift, risking immediate entry.

The dense clouds of the nebula can hide derelict ships, abandoned research stations, or temporary outposts. Characters may come across wrecks or structures containing useful resources, but these areas often have failing life support or residual radiation. 2.Nebula-Dwelling Entities: Strange lifeforms adapted to the nebula environment may dwell within the clouds. These entities might be curious or territorial, attacking if threatened. Characters must make Charisma (Animal Handling or Persuasion) checks (DC 15) to calm or communicate with them.

Powerful gusts of wind strike without warning, forcing ships or characters to make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) every 10 minutes or be blown off-course, colliding with nearby obstacles (1d6 bludgeoning damage).

•Characters can propel themselves in a direction by pushing off an object, moving 30 feet per push. Without something to grab onto, they drift in the same direction until stopped. •Maneuvering with a propulsion device (e.g., thruster pack) requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 13) to avoid spinning out of control. 2.Tethering and Anchoring: •Tethers are essential to prevent drifting away in the void. Tethered movement allows characters to maintain control, while untethered movement requires Dexterity checks (DC 14) to change direction or stop. •Using magnetic boots or grappling hooks to secure a position prevents drift and can stabilize movement on larger structures, like space debris or derelict ships. 3.Orientation and Navigation: •Without landmarks, characters must succeed on Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 15) to maintain orientation. Failure means they become disoriented, potentially drifting off course or struggling to find their bearings.

The stationʼs complex systems occasionally malfunction. Every few hours, roll a d20. On a 1 or 2, a localized power surge or system glitch occurs, temporarily disabling lights, ventilation, or gravity in that area for 1d6 minutes.

Radiation is common in certain parts of the nebula, posing a danger to unprotected travelers. Roll a d20 every hour; on a result of 1-5, the area contains high radiation, forcing a Constitution saving throw (DC 14) or causing 1 level of exhaustion.

The stationʼs automated defenses, such as turrets or drones, may still be active but faulty, treating all movement as a threat. Players must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to dodge attacks or succeed on Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 15) to shut down or reprogram the systems.

Gangs control different parts of the lower city. Characters entering gang territories must either pay a toll, fight, or negotiate with gang leaders. Encounters with street gangs may involve ambushes or bribes.

Characters may encounter ships trapped in time, appearing suddenly or flickering in and out of reality. These vessels may contain valuable data but risk dragging explorers into time dilation zones. Entering or interacting with these ships requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid getting caught in temporal shifts.

Moving through the interiors of larger wrecks poses risks of structural collapse. Characters navigating these spaces must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) every 10 minutes or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage from falling debris.

Small hull breaches cause air to leak into space. Characters near an air leak must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 14) to avoid being pulled toward it. Sealing a leak requires Intelligence (Engineering) checks (DC 15) and appropriate tools.

In marketplaces and hidden alleys, black market dealers offer rare items, though often at high prices or under dubious conditions. Negotiating a deal may require Charisma (Persuasion) checks (DC 14) to avoid price gouging or deception.

Massive, floating life forms unique to gas giants can emerge from the clouds. These creatures may be curious, territorial, or hostile. Characters must make Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks (DC 14) to calm or avoid these entities, or prepare for defensive maneuvers.

In the heart of storms, lightning strikes can disable electronics or damage hulls. Roll a d20 every 5 minutes in stormy areas; on a roll of 1-5, a lightning strike targets a nearby object. Characters or ships must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid taking 3d6 lightning damage.

•Moving through crowded markets and alleys requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12) to avoid pickpockets and muggers. Characters must also make Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 13) to avoid being marked by potential thieves. •In gang territories, characters may need to make Charisma (Persuasion) checks (DC 14) to negotiate safe passage or find alternate routes to avoid conflict.

•Moving through floating wreckage requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid collisions. Failing these checks results in 1d6 bludgeoning damage from debris impacts. •Characters exploring unstable ships must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid falling or being injured by shifting wreckage.

•Crowded Areas: Moving quickly through dense crowds (e.g., marketplace or entertainment district) requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12) to avoid bumping into others or causing commotion. •Security Checkpoints: Restricted areas are guarded by checkpoints requiring successful Charisma (Persuasion) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks (DC 15) to pass without authorization.

•Pilots navigating strong winds must make Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 15) every 10 minutes. Failure results in loss of control or drift, potentially placing the ship closer to dangerous storms or gas creatures. •On-foot navigation in a floating colony during strong winds requires Strength saving throws (DC

•Ships passing near wormholes must make Dexterity (Piloting) checks (DC 15) every 10 minutes to avoid gravitational pulls from unintended portals. Failure results in the ship being dragged into a random wormhole exit point. •Characters moving on foot through zero gravity must succeed on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) every 10 minutes to avoid drifting into unstable rifts or getting pulled by gravitational pulses.

Pirates hide near wormhole exit points to ambush travelers. They demand tolls, salvage tech, or attempt to steal wormhole data. Characters must make Charisma (Intimidation or Persuasion) checks (DC 15) to negotiate or Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to evade ambushes.
